properties.statement:
AFTER THE THREE APPROVED PERF CHANGES: THE MULTIPLIER IS GONE, TWO BUDGETS HOLD, AND THE ORIENTATION-PASS BUDGET MISSES ON A DERIVATION ERROR I MADE, NOT ON THE CODE. Measured 2026-09-05, reflow2-mcp 0.47.1 release built with all three changes, on a copy of the live store (105 MB, six real sync targets), stdio, load settling from ~2.5, medians.

THE THREE CHANGES (dec:the-loop-speaks-on-loop-status-not-inside-every-read; dec:an-unchanged-sync-target-is-not-re-parsed; dec:derived-scans-are-memoised-per-write-generation):
  1. reads stop recomputing loop_status for a debt hint.
  2. an unchanged sync target is answered from a stored (hash,len,mtime,nodes) observation, not re-parsed.
  3. open_defects and detect_gaps are memoised per write generation, the generation living on ReadCache so every backend write moves it.

BUDGETS:
  ✅ con:a-read-after-a-write-costs-at-most-twice-the-same-read-warm — get_node after a write 5.3 ms vs warm 3.7 ms, RATIO 1.41 (was ~5,900). THIS IS THE HEADLINE: the read-side hint ran a full loop_status 9.5 times a session, 1.2-1.9 min/session hidden; that is gone.
  ✅ con:loop-status-warm-latency-ms — warm loop_status 1,912 ms vs 2,000 (was 12,502).
  ❌ con:a-full-orientation-pass-costs-at-most-8-seconds — warm sum 6,459 ms (under) BUT cold-start 11,103 ms (over). The cold pass is the honest session-start case.

⭐ THE MISS IS A DERIVATION ERROR, STATED PLAINLY. I derived 8,000 ms from 'the expensive scans are paid ONCE per graph state.' They now are — the memo works, loop_status computes the defect+gap scan and open_questions/graph_report reuse it. But I budgeted as if the shared scan were the WHOLE cost, and it is not: measured with the memo hot, graph_report is 2,825 ms of its OWN rendering, open_questions 1,931 ms of its own, detect_defects 2,838 ms of its own sweep-scope walk — none of that is open_defects. The scan is paid once as designed; the pass still exceeds 8,000 because the rollups' non-scan work was never in the budget.

⭐ AND THE COMMON CASE IS HONESTLY STILL ~6.3 s. loop_status AFTER A WRITE is 6,354 ms (was 12,502). The memo cannot help it — a write changed the graph, so the count must be recomputed, which is correct. Computing open_defects once over 3,709 nodes / 18,101 edges is intrinsically ~5 s. 'Warm loop_status' (1,912 ms) is the repeat-with-no-write case; most loop_status calls follow a write, so 6,354 ms is what a session usually waits.

🛑 WHAT IS DELIBERATELY LEFT UNDONE, and why it is not scope-creep: making the ONE scan faster is a different optimization from stopping it being repeated. Two levers remain, each needing its own hypothesis and Anthony's ruling per the optimize skill: (a) open_defects intrinsic ~5 s — the detectors walk the whole edge set per category; (b) graph_report ~2.8 s and detect_defects ~2.8 s of own cost. None was approved; none was started.

NET FOR A SESSION: the change that mattered most is the multiplier, and it is gone — a write no longer taxes the next read with a 6-12 s rollup, 9.5 times a session. loop_status itself is ~2x faster after a write and ~6.5x faster warm. The orientation pass is ~3x faster warm and ~2.8x faster cold, still over a budget that was set too low.

BOUNDS: one machine, 4 cores, release, stdio, live-store copy; load was 2-6 during the window and the numbers are medians, so treat them as ±20%. Instruments: tools/agent_surface_profile.py, tools/time_one_tool.py.
